reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) only broadly mentions investigating intermetallic phases, corrosion, and solid-solution structures in Mg-containing alloys, without providing specific prior observations that support the detailed mechanistic premises about diffusion-driven phase separation, elemental partitioning, oxide catalysis, or galvanic couple reduction.
premises: Non-equilibrium Mg-containing lightweight HEAs contain metastable solid-solution regions and dispersed intermetallic compounds.
Thermal annealing triggers diffusion-driven phase separation that precipitates stable intermetallic compounds.
These precipitates partition passivating elements to the surface/near-surface regions.
The evolved intermetallics catalyze formation of an adherent, protective oxide during high-temperature oxidation.
The evolved intermetallics reduce micro-galvanic couples, lowering corrosion in saline environments.
